title: Anthro Energy breaks ground on factory that could pave the road to solid-state batteries
summary: Anthro Energy has started construction on a factory in Louisville, Kentucky, capable of producing battery materials for over 300,000 electric vehicles. The facility, set to begin production in 2028, aims to supply domestic, China-free electrolytes to support the U.S. battery supply chain. Anthro's polymer electrolyte, Proteus, is designed to enable solid- and semi-solid-state batteries, addressing challenges like energy density, fire risk, and dendrite formation. The project received significant federal and state funding to scale production and overcome manufacturing hurdles.
key_points: Anthro Energy's Louisville factory will produce 25 GWh of electrolytes, supporting U.S. battery manufacturers seeking China-free materials.
The facility is strategically located within a 12-hour drive of 70% of U.S. battery production sites.
Anthro received $24.9M from the DOE and $18.4M in tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act, plus $2.3M in state incentives for 110 jobs.
Proteus, Anthro’s polymer electrolyte, can integrate into existing production lines and later transition to solid-state formulations.
Solid-state batteries promise higher energy density, reduced fire risk, and prevention of dendrite-related short circuits.
Anthro’s manufacturing process involves a liquid-to-solid electrolyte transition, enhancing cell strength and flexibility.
The startup aims to address scalability challenges that have hindered solid-state battery adoption in EVs, drones, and robotics.
